_README: Each mutation breaks ONE behaviour the fixture claims to cover. Aim them at distinct branches — a mutation that neuters the whole hook only proves the suite notices a corpse. `why` is printed in the run output, so write it as the thing that would be silently broken. A key names the file to mutate, resolved the same way run-fixtures resolves a hook. Add "suite": "<hook>" when the mutated file is a shared library, so the run exercises a suite that actually consumes it.

merge-grant.why: a negated request arms the grant, so "don't merge yet" makes a merge approvable
a clause break stops ending a negation, so "don't close 19 but merge 17" no longer arms
notification text counts as the user's words, so an agent's own "ready to merge" arms the grant
a subagent's hand-back counts as the user's words, so its "open the PR" arms the pr grant
a typographic apostrophe stops normalising, so a typed “don’t merge” arms the grant
a negated PR request arms the pr grant, so "don't open a PR yet" drops the PR prompt
the verb window never closes, so a PR mentioned anywhere after "open" arms the pr grant
a comma ends the negation again, so "Don't, please, merge this" arms the grant
only a fixed list negates, so "we shouldn't open a PR yet" arms the pr grant
open mid-clause reads as the verb again, so "list the open draft PRs" arms the pr grant
pull request stops reading as a PR, so "open a pull request against main" arms nothing
a block the strip leaves unbalanced counts as the user's words, so a hand-back quoting its own closing tag arms a grant

destructive-guard.why: an empty directory reads as the current one again, so `cd "$(…)" && git push` reads the session's branch
an escaped space resolves to a missing directory again, so `cd main\ wt && git push` reads the session's branch
a cd behind if/then/do/builtin/command/time stops moving the directory
a case pattern's `)` closes a subshell again, so a later bare push reads the parent directory
every `)` closes a subshell again, so `$((1+1))` pops the directory a cd set
pushd stops moving the directory, so `pushd <main> && git push` reads the session's branch
--git-dir and GIT_DIR= stop making the repository unresolvable, so a bare push through them reads the session's branch
--recurse-submodules stops consuming its value, so `git push --recurse-submodules check origin` reads `check` as the remote
a tags-only push defaults to HEAD again, so `git push origin --tags` from main hard-blocks
an unreadable destination stops standing for the checked-out branch, so `git push origin $(git branch --show-current)` from main passes
a separator glued to a force or delete flag hides it again, so `git push origin x -f;echo` skips the prompt
a colon refspec after the first counts as no delete, so `git push origin x :other` skips the prompt

pr-create-guard.why: the stack form stops being recognised, so a stack submit skips every check
the dirty-tree block on a stack submit becomes advisory instead of blocking
the working directory stops being resolved, so every git check reads the session repo
an unresolvable default branch goes back to blocking, asserting a zero diff nobody measured

replace.from:
if ! git "${GITC[@]}" rev-parse --verify --quiet "origin/${DEFAULT_BRANCH}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  exit 0
fi

pr-create-guard.why: the command stops being stripped, so the guard fires on its own trigger in a -m body
only the FIRST cd is read, so `cd a && cd b` grades the repo the command left

stateful-op-reminder.why: the command stops being stripped, so the reminder fires on its trigger in a -m body

_lib/strip-cmd.why: an executed heredoc is blanked again, hiding a real invocation behind three lines of shell

_lib/split-cmd-segments.pl.why: a completed substitution is discarded, hiding a nested destructive command
a substitution scope opener is omitted, so checkout directory state cannot be restored safely
a substitution cuts its enclosing segment again, so `git -C "$(…)" push` reaches no push check
process substitution stops being a substitution, so `diff <(git push origin main) x` passes

_lib/strip-quoted-args.pl.why: empty quote fragments stop composing executable tokens
exec-wrapped shells lose their executable heredoc bodies
backtick escape decoding corrupts a nested executable token
quoted substitutions are treated as data, hiding nested mutations
an ordinary heredoc loses its executable expansions
quoted heredoc delimiters stop suppressing literal body text
